items.label: A
items.critique: Flat, generic courtesy ('This is the home of', 'very grateful for your deeds') with no tactical detail; exactly the stiff, slightly redundant voice of Nox's house guards.

items.label: B
items.critique: Ceremonial guild boasting plus a dropped article ('can be dangerous place') - an unpolished slip a generator rarely makes; pure flavour, no task.

items.label: C
items.critique: Built to a template: blocked gate, named villain beyond, named authority and where to find him, then a 'later' line that reopens the way. 'By order of', 'by the Captain's leave' is a more formal, mannered register than Nox's guards.

items.label: D
items.critique: Clipped, punchy and readable, but same blocked-route/who-to-see/route-reopened skeleton and terse elided sentences ('Below's shut.') that read as a modern bark style.

items.label: E
items.critique: Crams monster, cause, villain, quest-giver and her hut into one bark; the double-hyphen dash and the closing 'watch for leeches' quip are tells.

items.label: F
items.critique: The cows punchline ('the ones that are left') is a good joke but a too-neatly placed one; the gate-shut/see-the-Mayor/gate-open loop matches the other generated barks.

items.label: G
items.critique: Jailer's patter with escalating warnings and a slightly clumsy page break; flavour without quest scaffolding, typical Nox.

items.label: H
items.critique: Gushing 'You must be the great [Class]... our beloved [Place]!', capitalised 'Mayor', comma splice in the bandit line - the earnest, exclamatory Nox chapter-opener voice.

items.label: I
items.critique: Atmospheric touches ('the stones still smoke') and a double-hyphen dash; again the closed-bridge/guildmaster/reopened template.

items.label: J
items.critique: The tidy-city rules list with the 'don't even think about wizardry' jab and the 'Oh, I forgot to mention' follow-up is Nox's dry humour exactly.

tells: New barks all follow one rigid three-beat template: route closed + monster/villain + named authority and where to find them; repeat line; route reopened. Westwood's guards mostly just set mood, warn or welcome and do not route the player so precisely.
Information density: new first lines pack who, what, where and whom-to-see into two or three sentences; Westwood's are thinner and more redundant.
Double-hyphen '--' dashes appear only in new texts.
New texts end on a crafted quip or sensory detail (leeches, smoking stones, leftover cows); Westwood's humour is broader and tied to the speaker's role (no wizardry, no loitering).
Westwood lines carry small grammatical slips and stock fantasy phrases ('legendary', 'beloved', 'great deed'); new lines are cleaner and more colloquial-modern ('Below's shut', 'I just stand here').
